chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: Berman French and Dr. Lochte, Hardy's doctor
summary: His brother-in-law Berman French played banjo; Dr. Lochte, who treated Hardy's tuberculosis, was married to his sister-in-law.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Berman French was my brother-in-law. He played with me a while. He played banjo too. Of my first marriage. He was my brother-in-law. Incidentally, from my first marriage, Dr. Lochte was married to my sister-in-law from my first marriage. And he was Emmet Hardy's doctor. See, Emmet developed tuberculosis and Dr. Lochte had done so well with a couple of boys that worked for Canal Bank, I think it was. And he did such a fine job with them. He had those boys out playing baseball again in two years. Henry, Dr. Lochte was, he got to be quite a heart and lung specialist for the government, I think, before his passing. And he went back in the service with the rank of Colonel at the Veterans Hospital in Biloxi over there. And, uh, Berman played for a short while. I don't know just how long he played. But he got to be pretty good. He got to be alright.
